artists.biography: Jesus Jones are a British alternative dance band. The Wiltshire-based group, formed in late 1988, recorded and performed in the late 1980s, throughout the 1990s, and into the 2000s. They are best remembered for their track, "Right Here, Right Now", an international hit and subsequently globally appropriated for promotional and advertising campaigns. They are also well-remembered for the songs "Real Real Real" and "International Bright Young Thing."

perplexity.description:
Liquidizer, released in October 1989 on SBK Records (with later releases on Demon Records), is the debut album by British band Jesus Jones. The album blends electronic and rock elements, characterized by driving guitar riffs, prominent use of samples, and energetic rhythms that reflect the band's innovative approach to the alternative rock scene of the late 1980s. Its sound is often described as a noisy, spontaneous fusion of styles, capturing the band's conviction and experimental spirit. The album features the hit singles “Info Freako,” “Never Enough,” and “Bring It On Down,” all of which helped establish Jesus Jones as a distinctive voice in the UK music landscape.

As the band’s first full-length release, Liquidizer set the foundation for Jesus Jones’s subsequent work, showcasing their signature blend of electronic textures and rock energy. The album reached #32 on the UK Albums Chart and eventually earned a Silver Disc for sales of over 60,000 copies. Critics noted its raw, energetic production and its ability to capture the zeitgeist of the era, with keyboardist Iain Baker describing it as a “quick blast” and a “noisy, sudden amalgamation” of influences. Liquidizer remains a significant debut, marking the arrival of a band that would go on to influence the Britpop and alternative rock movements of the 1990s.
